data.body:
CLOSE EVIDENCE — all five acceptance criteria re-verified against the MERGED tree. Worktree HEAD
== origin/main == d49fea41cc38 ("Scope the terraform fault-test deadline to hang", Gerrit 2677),
confirmed an ancestor of HEAD by `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, and
`rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev d49fea41cc38` resolves 5310-b51f-bba6-4e61.

AC1 — the shortened deadline is applied only when mode == "hang". MET.
  tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py:352-353
      if mode == "hang":
          monkeypatch.setattr(tc, "DEADLINE_SECONDS", 1.0)
  `pytest tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py -q` -> 24 passed, 1 skipped in
  5.65s, the same counts as before the change.

AC2 — the fixture child writes capture.json atomically. MET.
  tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py:137-139
      staging = capture.with_name(capture.name + ".partial")
      staging.write_text(recorded, encoding="utf-8")
      os.replace(staging, capture)
  so `capture.exists()` is a sound readiness predicate by construction; a kill at any deadline can
  no longer leave a zero-byte file for `json.loads` to choke on.

AC3 — seeded-defect proof recorded. MET, in the earlier comment on this ticket. Deleting the
  `len(stdout) > MAX_STDOUT or len(stderr) > MAX_STDERR` guard at
  src/rebar/grounding/terraform_corroborator.py:300-301 makes [overflow-worker_failure] fail with
  `AssertionError: assert 'config_inspect_schema_skew' == 'worker_failure'`, and restoring the
  guard returns all four params to green. The parametrization genuinely exercises the branch it
  is named for — which the failing CI job's coverage report showed it previously did NOT reach
  (line 301 listed UNCOVERED for the whole job).

AC4 — 12 consecutive load runs, all passing. MET, run just now at merged HEAD, exactly the
  command the criterion names (`pytest tests/unit/grounding/ -n 16 --dist worksteal
  --cov=src/rebar`), oversubscribed 16-way on an 18-core host already carrying other agents' work:
    run  1: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 40.18s      run  7: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 39.06s
    run  2: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 40.04s      run  8: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 45.32s
    run  3: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 39.59s      run  9: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 65.06s
    run  4: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 39.04s      run 10: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 65.25s
    run  5: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 40.08s      run 11: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 42.59s
    run  6: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 39.63s      run 12: 366 passed, 1 skipped in 47.05s
    RESULT: 0/12 runs failed
  The 65s runs at 9 and 10 are the contended ones and still passed, which is the point: the
  pre-fix failure mode was precisely contention-driven. Compare the pre-fix measurement recorded
  earlier: 8 of 30 runs failed (~27%) under 36x CPU oversubscription, matching the ~2/9 per
  ubuntu-cell rate seen in CI.

AC5 — make verify green before push. MET — 19950 passed, 25 skipped in 31m32s, exit 0, zero
  FAILED lines, on the three-commit stack whose tree hash is byte-identical to what was pushed.

Closing class: flaky. Per docs/ticket-model.md the class records why the bug closed, and `flaky`
is defined as "a nondeterministic/intermittent failure" — which is exactly what this was: an
intermittent, load-sensitive test failure, measured at 8/30 locally under load and 2/9 per ubuntu
cell in CI. It is recorded as `flaky` in the repo's sense that a flaky test is a BUG to
root-cause, not a retry: the mechanism was found (a 0.2s wall-clock budget imposed on three fault
modes whose child must run to completion, plus a non-atomic capture write inside the kill window),
fixed, and proven RED to GREEN with a seeded-defect check. `regression` does not fit — nothing
previously worked; the test raced from the moment it was written.
